**Park Ji‑sung** (박지성) – commonly known simply as **Ji‑sung Park** – is a retired South Korean professional footballer who is widely regarded as one of the most influential Asian players in European football history.

| Category | Details |
|----------|---------|
| **Full name** | 박지성 (Park Ji‑sung) |
| **Date of birth** | 25 March 1981 |
| **Place of birth** | Seoul, South Korea |
| **Position** | Midfielder (primarily a box‑to‑box/defensive midfielder) |
| **Height** | 1.78 m (5 ft 10 in) |

### Club Career Highlights
| Years | Club | Appearances | Goals |
|-------|------|-------------|-------|
| 1999–2000 | Suwon Samsung Bluewings (K League) | 30 | 2 |
| 2000–2001 | Ulsan Hyundai Horang‑i | 28 | 1 |
| 2001–2002 | FC Bayern München (Germany) | 0 | 0 *(did not break into the first team)* |
| 2002–2003 | FC Stuttgart (Germany) | 12 | 0 |
| 2003–2004 | FC Stuttgart (Germany) | 15 | 0 |
| 2004–2015 | Manchester United (England) | 292 | 13 |
| 2015–2017 | PSV Eindhoven (Netherlands) | 48 | 1 |
| 2017–2018 | FC Utrecht (Netherlands) | 20 | 0 |
| 2018–2020 | FC Utrecht (Netherlands) | 18 | 0 |

> **Key points:**  
> • He spent 11 seasons at Manchester United, becoming the club’s longest‑serving Asian player.  
> • Known for his relentless work rate, stamina, and ability to cover large areas of the pitch.  
> • Won three Premier League titles (2006–07, 2007–08, 2008–09), the FA Cup (2009–10), the League Cup (2008–09), and the UEFA Champions League (2007–08).  
> • Earned 100 caps for the South Korean national team, captaining them at the 2010 FIFA World Cup and the 2014 FIFA World Cup.  

### International Career
- **National team:** South Korea (1999–2018)  
- **Caps:** 100+  
- **Goals:** 4  
- **Major tournaments:** 2002, 2006, 2010, 2014 FIFA World Cups; 2000, 2002, 2004, 2006, 2010, 2014 AFC Asian Cups.  
- **Notable moments:** Scored a crucial goal against Spain in the 2010 World Cup group stage, helping South Korea advance to the knockout round.

### Legacy & Impact
- **Pioneer for Asian players in Europe:** His success paved the way for many other Asian footballers to join top European leagues.  
- **Work ethic icon:** Frequently cited as a role model for professionalism, humility, and dedication.  
- **Post‑retirement:** After hanging up his boots, he has been involved in various ambassadorial roles, coaching clinics, and media appearances promoting football in Asia.
